comment: CodeQL findings reviewed and accepted. Each entry accepts at most `max` results of `rule` in `path`; anything beyond that still fails CI. Changing this file needs review like any security decision.

accepted.reason: CSRF is disabled only on the three stateless chains: actuator (management port, never routed by the gateway), /v1 ingest (OAuth2 bearer JWT in the Authorization header, no cookies, SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS) and the deny-all fallback. CSRF needs ambient credentials (cookies) to exploit; none of these chains accept them. The cookie-based console chain keeps CSRF on (CookieCsrfTokenRepository + SPA handler), and tests/http/test_console.py asserts state-changing requests without the token are rejected.

A test that sets a temporary store-key file (pytest tmp_path) to 0640 on purpose, to assert that load_key refuses any key file not chmod 600. The production code (pqt_connectors refs.new_key) creates keys 0600 and refuses anything looser; the same test asserts that too.
